title: Table Games
about: Remembering the loud, unofficial dining hall traditions that slowly disappeared over the years.
description: This track remembers the spontaneous dining hall traditions that became part of the State Arts-In experience: cheering when a plate broke, tables chanting back and forth across the room, and breakfast milk cartons stacked into increasingly ridiculous towers. None of the games were official or planned, yet they became shared traditions simply because people kept playing them. As rules changed, many eventually disappeared, leaving behind memories of a dining hall that once felt louder, stranger, and more alive.
lyrics: Before the noise got pushed away,
Someone broke a plate by accident,
Because all of us were here.
Loud enough to shake the room.
They lived because we played them.
And the next group took the call.
One by one the room kept climbing
Till the chant had crossed the hall.
Loud enough to shake the room.
They lived because we played them.
At breakfast no one planned it.
A group just chose to try.
Each person grabbed two milks or six,
Sometimes three friends made a kingdom.
Sometimes two whole tables built a wall.
Loud enough to shake the room.
They lived because we played them.
Past the morning it was made.
If the mood and milk were right.
They just need people in the light.
Loud enough to shake the room.
They lived because we played them.
Year by year the rules closed in.
The milk towers all got dropped.
By the time my final year came,
But silence cannot erase a game
I can still hear table one
I can still see breakfast cartons
I can still feel every head turn
At the sound of breaking glass,
Then the whole room roar together
For a second from the past.
Except the people there with me.
Just a room that once was louder,
And the memory of the games.
Like so many good things do.
But table one is still here calling:
